LARIMER COUNTY  |  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT  
 
 
Director’s Office, P.O. Box 1190, Fort Collins, Colorado 80522-1190, 970.498.7690, Larimer.org 
 
 
 
 
 
Building Permit Fee Increase of 2.29% on July 1, 2026 
 
In 2008, the Board of County Commissioners passed a resolution authorizing the Building 
Division to annually adjust Building Permit Fee Schedule Tables 1-A, 1-B, 1-C, and 1-E based on 
the US Department of Labor/Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index (CPI) for 
the Denver-Boulder-Greeley, Colorado area. Based on this year’s 2.29% increase in the 
successor regional CPI, the Building Division will adjust those fee tables accordingly, effective 
July 1, 2026. 
 
Transportation Capital Expansion Fee Increase Effective 
October 1, 2026  
The adjustment in the fees each year reflects changes in road construction costs during the 
previous year and is based on the Colorado Construction Cost Index data compiled and 
reported by the Colorado Department of Transportation (CDOT). Since 1998, Larimer County 
has been collecting transportation capital expansion fees from new traffic generating 
development to be used for improvements to the road system to accommodate the increase in 
traffic generated by the new development.

Color, graphical rules and underlining are outside plain-text representation. The text separator | is present. This is not missing legal wording.
Raster inspection cannot certify Unicode encoding. Preserve native U+2019 apostrophes; no word-level ambiguity or substitution is necessary.

review_method: Atlas directly inspected the full 300 dpi raster displayed at 1376x1780, compared complete native text, and reproduced the native extraction with PyMuPDF 1.28.2 sort=False flags=195. Reviewer hashes independently checked. No material text, numeric or reading-order error found.
independence_note: Atlas source check was saved before Ebenezer011 delivery was available. It was not a blind Atlas transcription because Atlas had the candidate. Ebenezer reports procedural blind pass1 and caption-mediated Read plus crops; those are reviewer method claims, not a claim of independent human vision.
